title: Magnetically induced Circular Photogalvanic Effect in Symmetric Two-dimensional Materials
authors: Peng Liu, Fanhao Jia, Ruixue Li, Yuan Li, Igor Zutic, Gaofeng Xu
abstract: Photocurrents that depend on the helicity of the incident light can be generated in both bulk and low-dimensional materials lacking inversion symmetry, known as the circular photogalvanic effect (CPGE). We propose that by employing a magnetic effect, the limitation on the inversion symmetry broken materials can be overcome, such that helicity-dependent photocurrent can be generated in a symmetric material, i.e., a magneto-circular photogalvanic effect (MCPGE). As a proof of principle, we elucidate the mechanism of such an MCPGE through an effective Hamiltonian of a monolayer SbH on a magnetic substrate with an adjustable magnetization. Moreover, the associated response in optical absorption is analyzed, both single-particle and excitonic, through a Bethe-Salpeter equation to describe the Coulomb interaction in excitons. Our result broadens the mechanism of CPGE and opens new opportunities for optoelectronic devices.
summary: This paper proposes the Magneto-Circular Photogalvanic Effect (MCPGE), showing that magnetic coupling can induce helicity-dependent photocurrents in materials lacking inversion symmetry. By modeling monolayer SbH on a magnetic substrate, the authors use advanced calculations involving Berry curvature and excitonic responses to prove this effect, opening new avenues for optoelectronic device design.
main_problem: The primary goal is to generate a helicity-dependent photocurrent (CPGE) in materials that possess inversion symmetry, overcoming the typical requirement of broken inversion symmetry.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that applying magnetic proximity effects can break the necessary symmetries, leading to a measurable Magneto-Circular Photogalvanic Effect (MCPGE) in an otherwise symmetric material like monolayer SbH.
method: The mechanism is elucidated using a second-order response formalism derived from an effective Hamiltonian incorporating exchange and Rashba SOC terms. Optical absorption is analyzed via the Bethe-Salpeter equation.
model_or_system: The model system is a monolayer (ML) SbH placed on a magnetic substrate with adjustable magnetization, treated as a 2D material exhibiting proximity magnetism. The Hamiltonian includes bare band structure, exchange interaction ($H_{	ext{ex}}$), and Rashba SOC ($H_R$).
key_observables: Photocurrents dependent on light helicity ($ eta_{ij}(\omega)$ tensor components), Berry curvature ($\Omega_v^z$), and excitonic absorption spectra ($\alpha_{\pm}(\omega)$).
important_parameters: Substrate magnetization direction ($\hat{n}$), in-plane magnetic field angle ($	heta$), and out-of-plane component ($\phi$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a two-band model (lower CB/higher VB) for calculating the CPGE tensor, and uses approximations inherent in solving the Bethe-Salpeter equation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate band structure shifts (isoenergy contours) under magnetic fields, the evolution of Berry curvatures ($\Omega_v^z$), and the dependence of the CPGE tensors on the angle ($	heta$) of the applied field.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the concept of MCPGE in symmetric materials. It then details the theoretical framework using an effective Hamiltonian for ML SbH on a magnetic substrate. The core analysis involves calculating photocurrents via Berry curvature and analyzing optical responses through BSE, culminating in demonstrating how magnetic asymmetry enables the effect.
why_interesting: The work provides a clear mechanism to engineer optoelectronic response by controlling symmetry breaking using magnetism, which is highly relevant for designing novel quantum light-matter interaction devices.

Spintronics.note: The paper explicitly discusses Magneto-Circular Photogalvanic Effect (MCPGE) in proximity-magnetized 2D materials using optical absorption and magnetic coupling, directly addressing the interface between quantum optics concepts and spintronic/magnetic systems.
